card.statement:
Let $V=V(a_1, a_2, a_3, a_4, \xi)$. Then

- [1.] $V$ is a $\mathfrak{g}$-module if and only if $V=V_1(a_1, a_2, a_3, \xi)$, with $a_3 \notin \mathbb Z$, or $V=V_2(a_1, a_2, a_3, a_4, -4)$.

- [2.] The $\mathfrak{g}$-module $V$ is a torsion free $\Gamma$-pointed $\mathfrak{g}$-module if and only if $S^{+}_{ijk}S^{-}_{ik}T^{-}_{jk}T^+_{k} \neq 0$, for all $i,j,k  \in \mathbb Z$.

- [3.] The torsion free $\Gamma$-pointed $\mathfrak{g}$-module $V$ is simple if and only if $Q^{+}_{jk}Q^{-}_{jk} \neq 0$, for all $ j, k  \in \mathbb Z$.

- [4.] If $V'$ is a simple torsion free $\Gamma$-pointed $\mathfrak{g}$-module with a basis parametrized by the lattice $\mathbb Z^3$ and with separating action of $\Gamma$ on basis elements, then $V'\simeq V(a'_1, a'_2, a'_3, a'_4, \xi')$, for some suitable choice of parameters such that $0 \le Re \, a'_1 < 1$, $0 \le Re \, a'_2 < 2$, $0 <   Re \, a'_3 < 2$, where $Re \, a$ denotes the real part of $a$.

- [5.] The action of the Casimir elements provides, in the case $a_3 = a_4$,

$$
z_{1}({\bf v}_{ijk}) =    \xi {\bf v}_{ijk} \quad \mbox{and} \quad
z_{2}({\bf v}_{ijk}) =   -\frac{1}{4} \xi(\xi+4) {\bf v}_{ijk}     $$

and, in the case $a_3 \neq a_4$,

$$
z_{1}({\bf v}_{ijk}) =     ((a_3 - a_4)^2 - 4) {\bf v}_{ijk}\quad \mbox{and} \quad z_{2}({\bf v}_{ijk}) =  0\,. $$
card.label: Theorem 21

paper.title: Gelfand-Tsetlin modules for Lie algebras of rank $2$
paper.abstract: We explicitly construct families of simple modules for Lie algebras of rank $2$, on which certain commutative subalgebra acts diagonally and has a simple spectrum. In type $A$ these modules are well known generic Gelfand-Tsetlin modules and they can be viewed as such for other rank $2$ Lie algebras.
